So I lay on all this shore Of Corinth a high feast for evermore And rite, to purge them yearly of the stain Of this poor blood. And I, to Pallas' plain I go, to dwell beside Pandion's son, Aegeus.--For thee, behold, death draweth on, Evil and lonely, like thine heart: the hands Of thine old Argo, rotting where she stands, Shall smite thine head in twain, and bitter be To the last end thy memories of me.

Hath Precinct Holy, That No Angry Men May Break Their Graves and Cast Them Forth Again to
Evil. So, I Lay on all this Shore of Corinth a High Feast for Evermore and Right, To Purge

Medea, never! Myself will lay them in a still green sepulcher, where Hera by the hill hath
precinct holy, that no angry men may break their graves and cast them forth again to evil.
So I lay on all this shore of Corinth a high feast for evermore and right, to purge them
yearly of the stain of this poor blood. And I to palace plain I go, to dwell beside
Pandian sun, Aegius. For thee, behold, death drawth on, evil and lonely, like thine heart.
The hands of thine old Argo, rotting where she stands, shall smite thine head in twain,
and bitter be to the last end thine memories of me.
